summary: Core change-event and public provenance bounds are separate contracts. Nullable core lower bounds need not alter public exports. Preserve operation-specific sample/absence endpoints and handle contradictory chronology explicitly. Source-only preflight, not acceptance.

findings.claim: Without a prior row, insertChangeEvent sets occurred_start equal to occurred_end. First observation (baseline/create/scope-enter) establishes presence by the sample time, not exact creation then; the non-null schema forces fabricated lower-bound precision.
findings.recommendation: Make change_events.occurred_start nullable: NULL means no supported lower bound, not zero-duration occurrence. Retain an applicable prior observation only when it supports this change/binding and is no later than the upper bound. Keep actual sample/absence occurred_end and publication detected_at; do not substitute scan start, mtime or completion as invented lower evidence.

findings.claim: No scoped consumer reads change_events.occurred_start/end as occurrence. Its readers join object/event identity or order by detected_at/events.observed_at. ProvenanceInput/Claim independently default omitted bounds to event.observedAt; provenance_claims bounds drive exported intervals and session/window overlap. EvidenceStoreEvent carries no occurrence interval.
findings.recommendation: Keep the core correction separate: it cannot fix public occurrence precision. Public unknown bounds would require coordinated provenance model, payload/schema and overlap-query changes; required-date v2 cannot accept NULL unchanged.

findings.claim: Rename-plus-growth deliberately has different upper bounds: rename uses max(new-path sample, old-path absence), growth uses the metadata sample. If prior observedAt exceeds that sample, insertChangeEvent permits an inverted growth interval even when rename remains ordered. Example prior=40, sample=30, absence=50 gives growth [40,30] and rename [40,50].
findings.recommendation: Reject contradictory chronology or retain an unknown lower bound with a limitation; never swap endpoints. Test prior=10/sample=20/absence=30/publication=40: rename end=30, growth end=20, both detected=40; separately test stale-sample inversion. Preserve these independent endpoints.

findings.claim: change_events currently requires both bounds, while genuine v5/v6 fixtures already contain a no-prior baseline with start=end. Historical sample times were not retained, so migration cannot reconstruct precise physical occurrence from run completion.
findings.recommendation: In unreleased v9, transactionally rebuild change_events with nullable start and an ordering check, preserving keys/FKs, deltas, detection/end fields and index. NULL historical no-prior starts; handle inversions explicitly. Keep noninverted prior-derived ranges as legacy estimates, not verified samples. Extend genuine v5/v6 fixtures with no-prior, prior-backed and inverted rows; assert NULL semantics, unchanged provenance, FK/index/cascade integrity, reopen idempotence and existing migration-failure recovery.
